body.statement:
Put \(D=Sd\).  Every nonempty class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) necessarily has \(B\ge D^2\).  Fix a nonempty compatible configuration of all fixed class constants.  If \(B>D^2\), then for each \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\) there are pairs
\[
(P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\subset
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)
\]
such that \(P_{\ell,q}(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\mid E_0)\ge c_X\), their conditional joint observed-data testing affinity is uniformly bounded away from zero,
\[
\inf_{N,T,\mathbf n}\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}>0,
\]
and
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,q}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,q}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_q
\quad\text{on }\mathcal Z_+,
\]
where \(R_q\) uses \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) in the spacing channel.  The treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, and donor pairs may additionally be chosen with uniformly bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence.  For the spacing pair only positive testing affinity is asserted.  Every pair is induced by a regular conditional law of the complete causal panel; in particular, its event means are stable given the complete historical design and its historical errors are centered given that design.  If \(B=D^2\), all the preceding assertions hold for \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp}\}\), but no universal donor-channel pair is asserted.  If \(B<D^2\), the class is empty and no minimax assertion is made.  Constants in the donor construction may depend on the fixed interior slack \(B-D^2\).
body.justification: Four same-class causal-panel pairs are constructed with fixed strict donor-envelope slack; the three non-donor pairs also hold at the compatible boundary.
body.gap: Nonemptiness yields \(B\ge(Sd)^2\), not strict slack. The common-support donor probability perturbation is proved only for fixed \(B>(Sd)^2\), with constants allowed to depend on the slack.
body.consumer: Lower-bound consumers use four channels in the interior-compatible regime and exactly three at equality.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(D=Sd\) and work throughout with a regular conditional experiment given \(E_0\).  The compatibility restriction follows before any lower-bound construction is attempted.  For every class member define, only in this proof,
\[
Y=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0).
\]
By the definitions of \(z_0\) and \(\Sigma\), and by \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity},
\[
\mathbb E_P[YY^\top\mid E_0]=I_D.
\]
Taking traces and then applying Jensen's inequality to the nonnegative random variable \(\|Y\|_2^2\) gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]
=\operatorname{tr}(I_D)=D,
\qquad
D^2
=\{\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]\}^2
\le \mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^4\mid E_0]
\le B,
\tag{1}
\]
where the last inequality is \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.  Thus \(B\ge D^2=(Sd)^2\) is necessary for nonemptiness.  Equality in Jensen at \(B=D^2\) forces \(\|Y\|_2^2=D\) almost surely.  In particular, nonemptiness does not imply the strict slack needed to perturb a common-support donor distribution.

We next give a causal completion used by all applicable channels.  Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
Choose the event path in a fixed compact subset of \(\mathcal Z_+\) contained in the interior of \(([0,1]^d)^S\).  Conditional on \(\mathscr X\), draw the bounded historical response paths independently across \((s,i)\), from kernels that may vary with \((s,i)\) and satisfy
\[
\mathbb E_P[Q_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=m_s(X_{st}).
\tag{2}
\]
Draw the observed event outcomes independently of \(\mathscr X\), also independently across units.  Then, with \(\varepsilon_{sti}=Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{3}
\]
Complete the unobserved event-date untreated outcomes so that their cohort-average conditional means equal \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Set observed and historical potential outcomes according to \texttt{ass:consistency} and \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}; make historical potential outcomes invariant to event treatment and all potential outcomes invariant to other units' assignments.  This verifies \texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}, \texttt{ass:no-spillovers}, and \texttt{ass:event-transport}.  Set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Equation (3) verifies the two additional restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).  Donors are chosen conditionally independently of this panel and identically over \(j\).

For the three non-donor channels and either compatible value \(B\ge D^2\), a common admissible donor law is explicit.  Let \(Y\) be uniform on
\[
\{\pm\sqrt D e_k:1\le k\le D\},
\]
where \((e_k)_{k=1}^D\) is the standard basis, and put \(Z_j=z_0+Y_j\) for conditionally independent copies \(Y_j\).  Direct summation yields
\[
\mathbb E[Y]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[YY^\top]=I_D,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|Y\|_2^4]=D^2\le B.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the full covariance is \(I_D\), which lies in the declared ellipticity envelope because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), and (4) verifies the fourth-moment condition even at the boundary \(B=D^2\).

We use the elementary binary relative-entropy bound
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le C_\eta v^2
\quad\text{whenever }p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta].
\tag{5}
\]
Indeed, the second derivative with respect to the first argument is \(1/\{u(1-u)\}\), so (5) follows from Taylor's theorem on the displayed compact interval.

For the treated channel, use an independent uniform historical design and choose the common regression carrier in the interior of \([0,B]\): take an affine carrier with nonzero standardized slope when \(\lambda\ge1\), and an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp when \(0<\lambda<1\).  Fixed rescaling within the nonempty class envelopes verifies \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness} and \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}.  Write
\[
V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{s=1}^S\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\qquad
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\),
\[
|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\le c_0.
\]
Choose fixed baseline event-response probabilities in \([2\eta,1-2\eta]\), and change only the treated event-response probability in cohort \(s\) by \(v_s\).  Taking \(c_0\) sufficiently small keeps all probabilities in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  The historical surfaces, donor law (4), and all other observed laws remain fixed.  Absorbing a fixed positive wealth scale into \(c_0\), \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and (5) give
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)-
  \tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)|
=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\tag{6}
\]
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{tr}},P_{0,\mathrm{tr}})
\le C\sum_{s=1}^Sn_sv_s^2
=Cc_0^2.
\tag{7}
\]

For the smoothing channel, choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\), and set
\[
b=c_b(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}.
\]
For a fixed compactly supported \(\lambda\)-Holder bump \(\psi\) with \(\psi(0)=1\), perturb only that cohort by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi\!\left(\frac{x-z_{0s_*}}b\right).
\tag{8}
\]
Choose as common carrier an interior-range affine surface with nonzero covariance-standardized gradient if \(\lambda\ge1\), and an interior-range asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp if \(0<\lambda<1\).  Choose it with fixed slack in the Holder and two-sided-modulus envelopes.  For a displacement of Euclidean size \(\delta\), the increment of (8) is at most \(Cc_1\delta^\kappa\): this is the scaled Holder bound for \(\delta\le b\), while for \(\delta>b\) it follows from \(b^\lambda\le C\delta^\kappa\).  Hence a sufficiently small fixed \(c_1\) preserves the response range, Holder ball, and both sides of the local-modulus condition.  With independent uniform historical design, the bump support has probability at most \(Cb^d\).  Since \(S\) is fixed, (5) and the maximizing choice imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-
  \tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)|^2
&=c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\\
&\ge c\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s^2
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=cR_{\mathrm{sm}},
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}
\le C.
\tag{10}
\]

For the spacing channel, invoke \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}.  Its rare-active-block construction has design-only geometric mixing, the required marginal density, full-design centering, and the two-sided modulus, and gives
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,\mathrm{sp}},dP_{1,\mathrm{sp}}\}
\ge a_{\mathrm{sp}}>0,
\qquad
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)-
  \tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{11}
\]
At \(B=D^2\), use (4) as the common donor marginal in that construction; donors carry no spacing-channel information, so this replacement changes neither affinity nor target separation.  Thus (11) is valid at both compatible envelope values.  Only affinity, not a Kullback--Leibler bound, is asserted in this channel.

It remains to construct the donor channel, for which assume the fixed interior-compatible slack \(B>D^2\).  Choose \(a_0>1\) so close to one that
\[
D^2+D(a_0^2-1)<B.
\tag{12}
\]
Let the coordinates of \(W=(W_1,\ldots,W_D)^\top\) be independent with
\[
P(W_k=a_0)=P(W_k=-a_0)=\frac1{2a_0^2},
\qquad
P(W_k=0)=1-\frac1{a_0^2}.
\tag{13}
\]
Every atom of the finite Cartesian support has positive probability.  Moreover,
\[
\mathbb E[W]=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(W)=I_D,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|W\|_2^4]
=Da_0^2+D(D-1)
=D^2+D(a_0^2-1)<B.
\tag{14}
\]
The strict inequality in (14) is precisely where the fixed slack \(B-D^2\) is used.

Choose a coordinate \(k_0\) belonging to a cohort \(s_0\).  For \(|\delta|\) small, alter only the three probabilities of \(W_{k_0}\) to
\[
p_+(\delta)=\frac{1+\delta^2}{2a_0^2}+\frac{\delta}{2a_0},
\quad
p_-(\delta)=\frac{1+\delta^2}{2a_0^2}-\frac{\delta}{2a_0},
\quad
p_0(\delta)=1-\frac{1+\delta^2}{a_0^2}.
\tag{15}
\]
All probabilities remain positive for sufficiently small \(|\delta|\), their sum is one, and
\[
\mathbb E_\delta[W_{k_0}]=\delta,
\qquad
\mathbb E_\delta[W_{k_0}^2]=1+\delta^2,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_\delta(W_{k_0})=1.
\tag{16}
\]
Independence of the other centered coordinates therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E_\delta[W]=\delta e_{k_0},
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_\delta(W)=I_D.
\tag{17}
\]
Let \(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+c_2N^{-1/2}e_{k_0}\), put \(\delta=c_2N^{-1/2}\), and under law \(\ell\) set \(Z=z^{(0)}+W\) with probabilities (13) for \(\ell=0\) and (15) for \(\ell=1\).  Equations (16)--(17) give the required two means and covariance \(I_D\) on one common finite support.  The map
\[
\delta\longmapsto
\mathbb E_\delta[\|W-\delta e_{k_0}\|_2^4]
\]
is continuous.  By the strict inequality in (14), taking \(c_2\) sufficiently small, with the permitted choice depending on \(B-D^2\), keeps this standardized fourth moment below \(B\) for every \(N\).  Thus covariance and fourth moment remain inside their envelopes.  Taylor expansion of the three-category relative entropy around the interior probability vector (13) yields
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN\delta^2
\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{18}
\]

For \(\kappa=1\), choose the weighted regression carrier to have a nonzero affine slope in direction \(e_{k_0}\).  For \(0<\kappa=\lambda<1\), in cohort \(s_0\) use
\[
x\longmapsto c_3
+c_4|e_{k_0}^\top(x-z_{s_0}^{(0)})|^\lambda
+c_5|e_{k_0}^\top(x-z_{s_0}^{(1)})|^\lambda,
\qquad c_4,c_5>0,quad c_4\ne c_5.
\tag{19}
\]
Fixed rescaling puts the carrier inside the response and Holder envelopes.  At either center, move along the coordinate ray pointing away from the other center.  Both cusp increments then have the same sign, and the cusp centered at the starting point has magnitude \(c_4\delta'^\lambda\) or \(c_5\delta'^\lambda\).  The Holder bound supplies the reverse upper inequality.  Since \(\Sigma=I_D\), this verifies the two-sided standardized modulus at both centers for \(0<\delta'\le\delta_0\).  Evaluation at the two centers gives
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s
\{m_s(z_s^{(1)})-m_s(z_s^{(0)})\}\right|
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{20}
\]
Keep the historical observed law, its surface, and the observed event mean fixed across the donor laws.  Complete the unobserved untreated event outcomes under law \(\ell\) with cohort means \(m_s(z_s^{(\ell)})\).  By \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, (20) is a causal-target separation, so
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{don}}}(z_0)-
  \tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{don}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cN^{-\kappa}=cR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{21}
\]

For completeness, bounded divergence implies positive testing affinity here by an elementary calculation.  Let \(p_1,p_0\) be densities with respect to a common dominating measure, put \(\phi(x)=x\log x\), and let \(A=\{p_1\ge p_0\}\).  Convexity of \(\phi\), applied separately on \(A\) and \(A^c\) with probability measure proportional to \(p_0\), gives
\[
\int p_0\phi(p_1/p_0)
\ge \operatorname{kl}\{P_1(A),P_0(A)\}.
\]
The two Bernoulli probabilities differ by \(\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Taylor expansion of binary relative entropy in its first argument, whose second derivative is at least four, therefore gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)
\ge2\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}^2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\ge1-\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2}.
\tag{22}
\]
Reducing the fixed constants \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (22) uniformly positive in the treated, smoothing, and, when \(B>D^2\), donor channels; (11) supplies spacing affinity.  The constants in the donor channel may depend on the fixed slack \(B-D^2\).  The event path is chosen in \(\mathcal Z_+\) with conditional probability one.  Equations (2)--(4), the channelwise calculations, and the causal completion verify every member property of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).  Thus all four pairs exist when \(B>D^2\), while (4), (6)--(11) give exactly the three asserted pairs when \(B=D^2\).  Equation (1) shows that \(B<D^2\) yields no class member, and no donor-channel converse has been asserted at equality.
